fieldMarks: Very large, slender cat with a small head and small rounded ears without tufts.
Uniform grizzled gray to tawny, cinnamon or rufous upperparts; whitish underparts, chin and throat.
Long, heavy, cylindrical tail about one-third of total length, with the last 2-3 in black.
Black sides of the muzzle and black behind the ears; pinkish nose.
Males 79-265 lb, females 64-141 lb; total length 5-8.5 ft.
behavior: Solitary and primarily nocturnal, though sometimes active by day; climbs trees readily.
Ambush predator that stalks and attacks at close range; deer are the main prey, also elk and smaller mammals.
Caches large kills under leaves and debris, dragging them up to 350 m, and returns nightly to feed.
Marks territory with scrapes, urine and scat; vocalizations include hisses, growls, yowls and screams.
habitat: Areas with dense cover or rocky, rugged terrain and low human population, from mountain conifer forest to grassland, brush country and swamps.
range: Historically ranged coast to coast in North America and north to southeastern Alaska. Now largely restricted to mountainous, sparsely populated areas, expanding in the western United States; eastern populations were exterminated except a small Florida panther population. Lions confirmed farther east, such as in Missouri, are likely wanderers from the west, and eastern sightings outside Florida are often escaped captive cats.

lookalikes.name: Bobcat
lookalikes.howToTell: Bobcat is much smaller with a short tail and a spotted, streaked coat rather than uniform colour.
